Select unrelated individuals with a target composition

Source: R/rkn_select_global.R
rkn_select_global.Rd

Selects a set of unrelated individuals whose composition, over the whole selection, is as close as possible to a target: the proportion of one category of a categorical covariate, such as the proportion of women, or the mean of a numeric covariate, such as the mean age. The set has the largest possible size, as a maximum set (see rkn_selection), unless max_loss allows a smaller one in exchange for a closer composition. Unlike rkn_select_criteria, which applies its criteria within each family, the families are chosen jointly: the choice in one family depends on what the others contribute. For instance, with ten unrelated women and ten related pairs of a woman and a man, choosing within each pair gives fifteen women on average, while choosing the man in every pair gives ten women and ten men.

Usage

rkn_select_global(
  g,
  covariate,
  target = NULL,
  max_loss = 0,
  resolution = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  diagnostics = TRUE
)

Arguments

g

An igraph object. Vertex names must be stored in V(g)$name. Vertex attributes cannot be named degree, max_path_length or .name: these names are reserved for the structural measures computed during the selection. The network is usually built with rkn_graph_from_kinship, which also checks the samples; for a network built in another way, see rkn_check_samples.

covariate

Character. Name of a vertex attribute of the network, either categorical (character, factor or logical), such as "sex" for V(g)$sex, or numeric, such as "age".

target

For a categorical covariate, the target proportion of one category among the selected individuals, named by the category, e.g. c(F = 0.5); for a covariate with two categories, the proportions of both may be given, summing to 1, and the first is used. For a numeric covariate, the target mean, a single unnamed number, e.g. 45. If NULL (default), the target is the composition of the whole network, so that the selection keeps that of the cohort: the mean, or the proportion of the first category, which is TRUE for a logical covariate, the first level for a factor, and the first in alphabetical order otherwise; for a categorical covariate this requires two categories.

max_loss

Non-negative integer. Largest number of individuals that may be selected below the maximum, to bring the composition closer to the target. With 0 (default) the selection keeps the maximum size. rkn_tradeoff shows, before selecting, the proportion or mean that each number of individuals given up allows.

resolution

For numeric covariates only, a positive number: the values are rounded to multiples of resolution above the smallest value to search the selections (see Details). If NULL (default), integer values spanning at most 100 are not rounded (a resolution of 1, e.g. for ages in years or scores); other values are rounded to the smallest of 1, 2 or 5 times a power of 10 that divides their range into at most 100 steps, e.g. 0.5 for values from 16 to 45, or 2000 for values from 0 to 200,000. If the tables of the search would then exceed the memory budget (see Details), as with ages in years in cohorts of about 100,000 samples, the default resolution is coarsened along the same sequence until they fit, and print() says so.

seed

Optional integer. If provided, the draw among the best selections is reproducible. If NULL (default), the current random number stream is used.

diagnostics

Logical. If TRUE (default), the returned object also records the family of each individual and, for each family, the individuals selected, those in the category or their mean, and those with a missing value (node_diagnostics and family_summary, see rkn_selection). Global selections have no types of decision, so that summary() shows no decision table and plot(type = "diagnostics") draws the selected and discarded individuals instead.

Value

An object of class rkn_selection with method = "global"; its element global describes the composition reached (see rkn_selection).

Details

The selection is chosen in three steps: first the proportion or mean closest to the target; then, among the selections that reach it, the largest; then one of the selections with that composition and that size, drawn uniformly at random. With max_loss > 0, individuals are given up even for a small improvement of the composition. The proportion or the mean is computed among the selected individuals with a known value of the covariate; the number of selected individuals with a missing value is reported by print().

The optimisation is exact. For each family, the exact algorithm described in the section Search over maximum sets of rkn_selection counts its sets of unrelated members by size and by number of members in the category, or by sum of the values; dynamic programming then combines the families. The counts are kept on the logarithmic scale, so that rare combinations, as for an extreme target, are not lost, and print() reports the number of selections reaching the best composition.

For a numeric covariate, counting the selections by sum of the values requires values on a grid: with values recorded to the day, almost every selection would have its own sum. The values are therefore rounded to multiples of resolution for the search only, and print() reports the mean of the recorded values of the selected individuals. Since the rounding moves the mean of any selection by at most half the resolution, the distance of the selected mean from the target exceeds the smallest possible by at most resolution; in practice the rounding errors of the individual values partly cancel, and the mean moves by much less than half the resolution when the resolution is fine compared with the spread of the values. They do not cancel entirely, because the values are seldom spread evenly between two multiples of the resolution. The time grows with the number of steps over the range of the values, and quickly with max_loss: a coarser resolution shortens it.

The computation of a family is not attempted when it would exceed a budget of memory and time, as for the largest families of genetic isolates at the third degree of relationship. Such a family contributes the maximum sets with the smallest and the largest number of members in the category, or sum of the values, found exactly or, in the most intricate families, among the maximum sets that remain after removing individuals who cannot enlarge the selection, and those of 100 uniform draws; a family too intricate even for this is selected as by rkn_select_random. The selection then keeps the maximum size, but the composition may not be the best possible and the draw is not uniform within these families, whose number print() reports. If the tables that combine the families would exceed about 800 MB, which requires many individuals with a missing value, a large max_loss or, for a numeric covariate, a fine resolution, the selection stops with an error before allocating them, unless the resolution of a numeric covariate was left to its default, which is then coarsened until the tables fit. The mean of the selection then lies within half the resolution of the mean that the search reaches, and usually much closer: in a synthetic cohort of 100,000 samples, with ages rounded to 10 years, the selected mean was 50.07 for a target of 50. The work of these tables is also estimated beforehand: beyond about half a minute on a recent laptop, a message warns that the selection may take several minutes, and a smaller max_loss or a coarser resolution shortens it.

See also

rkn_tradeoff for the proportions or means reachable by each number of individuals given up; rkn_selection, rkn_select_criteria, rkn_select_random.

Examples

# A small relatedness network: two parents and their child (P1, P2, C1), a pair of
# siblings (S1, S2), three mutually related individuals (T1, T2, T3), a larger family
# (parents D1 and D2, their children K1 and K2, and K3, born to D2 and D3, a
# half-sibling of K1 and K2) and an unrelated individual (U1).
g <- igraph::graph_from_literal(P1 - C1 - P2, S1 - S2, T1 - T2 - T3 - T1,
                                D1 - K1 - D2, D1 - K2 - D2, K1 - K2,
                                D2 - K3 - D3, K1 - K3, K2 - K3, U1)
sex <- c(P1 = "F", C1 = "M", P2 = "M", S1 = "M", S2 = "F", T1 = "M", T2 = "F", T3 = "M",
         D1 = "M", K1 = "F", D2 = "F", K2 = "M", K3 = "F", D3 = "M", U1 = "F")
age <- c(P1 = 52, C1 = 21, P2 = 55, S1 = 34, S2 = 31, T1 = 60, T2 = 33, T3 = 29,
         D1 = 63, K1 = 35, D2 = 61, K2 = 38, K3 = 30, D3 = 58, U1 = 44)
igraph::V(g)$sex <- unname(sex[igraph::V(g)$name])
igraph::V(g)$age <- unname(age[igraph::V(g)$name])
# Half women among the selected
sel <- rkn_select_global(g, "sex", c(F = 0.5), seed = 1)
sel
#> <rkn_selection> Global selection (proportion of sex = F), seed 1
#> Call: rkn_select_global(g = g, covariate = "sex", target = c(F = 0.5), seed = 1)
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 8 (53.3%)
#> Families: 5 | size min/mean/max: 1 / 3.00 / 6
#> Families with up to 5 members: 4 | with 6 or more: 1
#> Proportion of sex = F among the selected: 0.5000 (4 of 8; target 0.5)
#> Selections reaching this proportion: 3, one drawn uniformly
sel$kept
#> [1] "P1" "P2" "S2" "T3" "D1" "D2" "D3" "U1"

# The proportion of women of the whole network
rkn_select_global(g, "sex", seed = 1)
#> <rkn_selection> Global selection (proportion of sex = F), seed 1
#> Call: rkn_select_global(g = g, covariate = "sex", seed = 1)
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 8 (53.3%)
#> Families: 5 | size min/mean/max: 1 / 3.00 / 6
#> Families with up to 5 members: 4 | with 6 or more: 1
#> Proportion of sex = F among the selected: 0.5000 (4 of 8; target 0.4667, the proportion of the network)
#> Selections reaching this proportion: 3, one drawn uniformly

# Give up to two individuals to get closer to 70% women
rkn_select_global(g, "sex", c(F = 0.7), max_loss = 2, seed = 1)
#> <rkn_selection> Global selection (proportion of sex = F), seed 1
#> Call: rkn_select_global(g = g, covariate = "sex", target = c(F = 0.7), max_loss = 2, seed = 1)
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 7 (46.7%)
#> Families: 5 | size min/mean/max: 1 / 3.00 / 6
#> Families with up to 5 members: 4 | with 6 or more: 1
#> Proportion of sex = F among the selected: 0.7143 (5 of 7; target 0.7)
#> Selected: 7 of a largest possible 8 (max_loss = 2)
#> Selections reaching this proportion and size: 5, one drawn uniformly

# A mean age of 45 years
rkn_select_global(g, "age", 45, seed = 1)
#> <rkn_selection> Global selection (mean of age), seed 1
#> Call: rkn_select_global(g = g, covariate = "age", target = 45, seed = 1)
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 8 (53.3%)
#> Families: 5 | size min/mean/max: 1 / 3.00 / 6
#> Families with up to 5 members: 4 | with 6 or more: 1
#> Mean of age among the selected: 49.12 (8 individuals; target 45)
#> Selections reaching this mean: 1, one drawn uniformly
